clue.text: One expected to fail, being poorly grounded

indicators.note: poorly means badly put together, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tipped to lose because they lack a proper foundation or training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges GROUNDED. The surface makes 'grounded' sound like 'well-founded'; really it is just the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider tipped to lose a contest is the classic underdog.

clue.text: Head for the drink

definitions.meaning: slang for a person's head or brain
a small measure of spirits, about a quarter of a pint

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the skull and an old word for a small tot of liquor share one spelling.

clue.text: Always with time to turn out

parts.note: always means for ever

explanation.surface: Someone who perennially has time to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' looks like 'attend'; here it means turn inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert an organ is to turn it inside out, a medical term.

clue.text: Sailor returning on leave? No, soldier!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes below it

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon

indicators.note: returning means the word for the sailor is read backwards

parts.note: tar is the old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman heading back from shore leave turns out to be an army man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the sailor around. 'No, soldier!' corrects the surface's naval guess. The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division, famed in the North African campaign of World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were a British armoured division, so one of its members was a soldier.

clue.text: Leave university, hurt, and paint

parts.note: to leave is to go
to hurt is to ache

explanation.surface: A student drops out, wounded, and takes up painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouache is an opaque watercolour, a kind of artist's medium.

clue.text: Hoard tons to obtain superior status

parts.note: a cache is a hidden hoard

explanation.surface: Amassing great quantities of wealth to gain prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means prestige or distinction.

clue.text: Long distance traveller that should arrive on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece on another goes beneath it

parts.note: to arrive is to come

explanation.surface: A long-haul passenger who ought to be punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a train or plane; the traveller is a celestial body crossing vast distances.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet travels huge distances around the Sun, returning on a schedule.

clue.text: Container wagon to drive across the north of Grampians

parts.note: a cart is a simple wagon

indicators.note: across means the ride word stretches over the letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: to ride is to drive along in a vehicle or on a horse

indicators.note: in a down clue the north of a word is its top, the first letter

explanation.surface: Driving a wagon across the Scottish Grampian mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts G (the north of Grampians) inside RIDE to give RIDGE. The Grampians are a mountain range in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a case holding ink, film or an explosive charge.

clue.text: Regular air service?

parts.note: regular means even or uniform
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A scheduled flight run by an airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air service' suggests aviation; it is a church service with music.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of prayers and canticles in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Flyers, for example, on test regularly dropped

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: regularly dropped means every other letter of the word test is removed

explanation.surface: Pilots who keep failing their flight examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly dropped' removes the alternate letters E and the second T from TEST, leaving TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are herons, so birds that fly.

clue.text: Prestigious riding stock, for example

parts.note: a jockey riding is up on the horse
the stock market is one kind of market

explanation.surface: Elite horse-riding livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riding stock' looks like horses; 'riding' is UP (in the saddle) and stock exemplifies a market.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods are high-class and exclusive.

clue.text: Landmark ruling on this — or struggle

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another goes after it
struggle means the letters wrestle into a new order

parts.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge, which means ruling

explanation.surface: A court decision on a matter of dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggle' rearranges the two clue words before the dash. 'Landmark ruling' reads as one phrase and as the definition, but 'ruling' is in charge, abbreviated, and only 'Landmark' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic event is significant enough to be a milestone.

clue.text: Half of them run when hearts beat

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the word's four letters are taken

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
as can mean when
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: Some people flee when their hearts are racing.
explanation.walkthrough: TH comes from the first half of 'them'.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone is to beat them soundly.

clue.text: Dealing in this — or garden design

indicators.note: design means the letters are laid out afresh in a new pattern

explanation.surface: Trading in this or in landscape gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-trading is shrewd bargaining, a kind of hard-nosed negotiation.

clue.text: Secured accommodation for a floating voter

definitions.text: Secured accommodation for a floating voter

parts.words: Secured accommodation for a floating voter
parts.note: a floating voter is literally someone who lives afloat, and their moored home is accommodation tied up securely

explanation.definitionFit: A home moored to a bank is a dwelling that floats.

clue.text: Organise some golf, getting evasive replies

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it
a round is a single session of golf

explanation.surface: Arranging a golf game while dodging questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given the runaround means being fobbed off with evasions.

clue.text: Lacking barriers, launch programme

parts.note: to launch something is to open it
a programme is a plan

explanation.surface: Launching an unrestricted scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan space has no internal walls.

clue.text: Net can be fitted in a quietly perfect accessory

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: in signals the anagram goes inside the word for perfect

parts.note: pure means perfect or flawless

indicators.note: be fitted suggests the letters are reassembled to fit

explanation.surface: A net that is installed perfectly makes a quiet, ideal accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be fitted' rearranges the opening pair to TENANC, and 'in' places it inside the word for perfect. The surface's 'quietly perfect' reads as one phrase, but each word gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An appurtenance is an accessory or appendage belonging to something.

clue.text: Fantasise menfolk are up to containing vengeance

indicators.note: are up says the hidden letters are read backwards, as in a down clue they are read upward
containing says the letters sit inside the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fantasising men are about to seek revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'containing vengeance' as the definition, but 'containing' is the hidden-word indicator, so only 'vengeance' defines. 'are up' reads SISEMEN upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so the word means just punishment.

clue.text: "I hear you smell" — a cry of discovery!

indicators.note: I hear says the words are to be said aloud

parts.note: to smell is to reek, so you smell gives you reek

explanation.surface: An insult about body odour presented as a scientific exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You reek' said aloud gives EUREK, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes is said to have shouted this Greek exclamation on discovering displacement in his bath.

clue.text: Eat at home? Sounds like a joke

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: sounds like says the next word is said aloud

parts.note: a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: Is dining at home a laughing matter?
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body.

clue.text: Time for everyone to pass on knowledge

parts.note: each means every one

explanation.surface: It is time for everyone to share what they know.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct.

clue.text: Bird that could spoil a fight

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A bird that might wreck a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: The marabou stork is a large African bird, of which this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Bush wants French cheese, right?

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A president wants French cheese, correct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the US president; it is a thorny shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier is a prickly shrub, such as the wild rose.

clue.text: 1 could be one of these after the race!

definitions.text: 1 could be one of these after the race!

parts.words: 1 could be one of these after the race!
parts.note: 1 refers to the answer at 1 across, a contestant tipped to lose, who after a race is one of the unplaced finishers

explanation.definitionFit: Horses that finish unplaced in a race are listed as non-winners.

clue.text: Joined journalist attached to small fighting force

indicators.note: attached to means the journalist piece is joined on after the other

parts.note: a unit is a small military group
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter embedded with a small military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined together.

clue.text: Partners with an urge to shop

parts.note: S and N are partners at bridge, south and north
an itch is an urge or craving

explanation.surface: Couples who have a desire to go shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' means inform on someone, British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To snitch is to inform on, as is the slang verb shop.

clue.text: Aspect true of the stars?

parts.note: a side is an aspect
real means true

explanation.surface: Is the astrological aspect accurate?
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal relates to the stars, as in sidereal time.
